name: Development
_comment_worktree: Two additions serve the isolated worktree runtime and nothing else. (1) runArgs publishes container port 8080 on a loopback-only host port taken from DEVENV_PUBLISHED_HOST_PORT, which scripts/worktree/ensure.sh exports from the generated worktree environment before it runs `devcontainer up`. When that variable is unset — the DevPod and editor path — the substitution collapses to `-p 127.0.0.1::8080`, which Docker accepts and answers with an ephemeral loopback port, so nothing that worked before needs the runtime to keep working. (2) containerEnv.DEVCONTAINER_WORKTREE_ENV_FILE points .devcontainer/environment.sh's existing worktree seam at the generated container-view environment; environment.sh itself is unchanged. Both live in .devcontainer, which is a definition-fingerprint input, so adopting them costs every existing container one rebuild.
_comment_warp: Warp ACP signals (TERM_PROGRAM, WARP_CLIENT_VERSION, WARP_CLI_AGENT_PROTOCOL_VERSION) are NOT forwarded here via remoteEnv ${localEnv:...} — that blanks out on every rebuild because DevPod resolves localEnv against its own (often GUI-launched) process env, which lacks Warp's per-terminal vars. Instead, the initializeCommand entry `capture-warp-env` runs .devcontainer/host/capture-warp-env.sh on the host to persist them to ~/.config/devcontainer/warp-env (visible in-container at /run/devcontainer-config/warp-env), and configs/.shell_common sources+exports that file in every interactive shell so Claude Code inherits it. Seed it by running `devpod up .` from a Warp terminal at least once.
_comment_secrets: Two-tier secrets — both files use KEY=value format (one per line, # for comments). (1) Common: ~/.config/devcontainer/secrets — loaded in every project; good for shared keys like GITHUB_TOKEN (raises proto/GitHub API rate limit from 60 to 5000 req/hr) and CONTEXT7_API_KEY. (2) Per-project: ~/.config/devcontainer/secrets.d/<DEVCONTAINER_PROJECT> — loaded only for this container; good for project-specific tokens. Per-project values override common ones when the same key appears in both. Update DEVCONTAINER_PROJECT to a short lowercase slug matching your project when creating a new project from this template. GITHUB_TOKEN is also auto-passed from the host shell via remoteEnv if already set there. Delivery: the unconditional initializeCommand entry `prepare-container-env` runs .devcontainer/host/prepare-container-env.sh, which validates both sources through the strict KEY=value parser and atomically writes the mode-0600 Docker env file named in runArgs (--env-file), so PID 1 and every process it spawns — including the editor extension host and MCP subprocesses — inherit the keys without any /etc/environment mutation. .devcontainer/environment.sh re-reads the same mounted sources on every shell bootstrap, so keys added after create reach new shells without a rebuild.
